author: Oscar Maung-Haley
title: Dolphins firing of Mike McDaniel 'is in sight' with interesting replacement candidate emerging - NewsBreak
text:
By Oscar Maung-Haley ,
39 minutes ago Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel could face the axe from the organization following their dismal 1-4 start to the campaign.
The 2025 NFL season is now underway, with the Dolphins managing just a single victory so far this year . This past Sunday witnessed them surrender a 17-point advantage to the Carolina Panthers, as Miami's defense allowed 206 rushing yards to running back Rico Dowdle in a crushing 27-24 loss.
Just seven days earlier, the Dolphins lost star wideout Tyreek Hill to a horrific injury , and although Darren Waller has delivered an offensive spark following his drama-filled retirement reversal, Miami appears headed for another disappointing campaign.
READ MORE: Tommy Fleetwood's opinion on Bryson DeChambeau clash after new Ryder Cup footage emerges
READ MORE: Travis Kelce could have another fine coming after Chiefs loss to Jaguars
Despite the Dolphins reaching the postseason in both of Mike McDaniel's initial two seasons at the helm in 2022 and 2023, they fell short last year after finishing 8-9. With their lackluster start to this season, McDaniel, who inked a three-year contract extension in 2024, may be shown the door in Miami.
Per Sportskeeda's Tony Pauline, Dolphins owner Stephen Ross will allegedly dismiss McDaniel if the squad fails to show competitiveness during their upcoming "6-7 games."
However, the more intriguing development concerns who has been mentioned for the position to succeed McDaniel. Pauline also indicates that one candidate who has been floated to take over from McDaniel is former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan.
The 62-year-old led the Jets to consecutive AFC Championship games in 2009 and 2010, marking the last time New York made it to the postseason. Ryan was let go by the Jets in 2014, only to become the Buffalo Bills' head coach less than a fortnight later.
However, his stint in Buffalo was short-lived, lasting just two seasons before he was shown the door again. Since then, he's been sharing his insights as an analyst for ESPN.
This Sunday, the Dolphins are hoping to turn their season around when they host the Los Angeles Chargers at Hard Rock Stadium.
The Chargers started the season strong with a 3-0 record, sparking Super Bowl contender chatter. However, they've stumbled in their last two outings against the New York Giants and Washington Commanders, compounded by a slew of injuries.
On Monday, it was announced that rookie first-round running back Omarion Hampton is on injured reserve due to an ankle injury. Offensive linemen Joe Alt and Mekhi Becton are also nursing injuries.
